subject: general
question: Sharad can complete a piece of work alone in 13 days and Varad can complete the same piece of work alone in 9 days. They started the work together, but Varad had to leave 11 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work complete?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 13 and 9) = 117 units.

If a person leaves **before completion**, add their potential work to the total.

Total units = 117 + (Varad's efficiency × days before completion) = 117 + (13 × 11) = 117 + 143 = 260 units.

Total days = Adjusted Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 260 ÷ (9 + 13) = 260 ÷ 22 = 130 ÷ 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11(9/11) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sharad takes 13 days, Varad takes 9 days. Varad leaves 11 days before completion.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **Sharad**
 13
 117
 9
 
 

 **Varad**
 9
 13
 
 

⇒ Let the total work be completed in **x days**.

⇒ Sharad worked for **x days** and Varad worked for **(x − 11) days**.

⇒ 9 × x + 13 × (x − 11) = 117

⇒ 9x + 13x − 143 = 117

⇒ 22x = 117 + 143

⇒ 22x = 260

⇒ x = 260 ÷ 22 = 130 ÷ 11 = 11(9/11)

**∴ The correct answer is 11(9/11) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leaving Before Completion

When a person leaves **n days** before completion, treat it as if they worked those **n days** by adding their work to the total LCM.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If time ratio is A:B, the efficiency ratio is B:A.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to work; however, **outlet pipes** have negative efficiency while **inlet pipes** have positive efficiency.</p
